councils.name: City of Bayswater

planning_scheme.name: City of Bayswater Local Planning Scheme No. 24

lodgement.label: Lodge through the City's eProperty online lodgement portal
Email your application as PDFs (a single email, 20MB maximum)
Hand in hard copies at the Civic Centre and pay by cash, eftpos or credit card
Post hard copies to
lodgement.address: City of Bayswater, PO Box 467, Morley WA 6943

steps: Prepare a signed application form, a certificate of title less than 6 months old, a cover letter and scaled plans (plus landscaping plans for commercial, grouped and multiple dwelling developments).
Lodge online, by email or as hard copies.
The City gives your application to an officer, who sends you an acknowledgement letter with a reference number.
The officer may ask for more information or changed plans, or refer it to other agencies. It may be advertised, usually for 14 days.
Expect a decision in 60 to 90 days. If it's refused, you can appeal to the State Administrative Tribunal.

pre_lodgement.note: For single houses and additions only, a Deemed-to-Comply Check costs $295 and takes 14 days. Email the Clause 61A form and plans to planning.referrals@bayswater.wa.gov.au.

Write a covering letter or report explaining your proposal and any variations you're asking for.

Get a certificate of title from Landgate and prepare the plans and information in the City's Planning Information Checklist.

councils.name: City of Vincent

planning_scheme.name: City of Vincent Local Planning Scheme No. 2

lodgement.label: Register, then lodge through the City's online portal (select Lodge Applications). Not available for Development Assessment Panel applications.

steps: Register for an account on the City's online portal, or sign in. Wait for the confirmation email.
Log in, select Lodge Applications and lodge your development application. For Development Assessment Panel applications, contact the City instead.
The City checks your application is complete and writes to you if anything is missing.
An Urban Planner assesses it, may ask for more information (usually within 14 days) and may notify neighbours for 14 to 21 days.
You're told the decision in writing. If you disagree, you can ask the State Administrative Tribunal to review it within 28 days.

pre_lodgement.note: The City offers Design Review Panel pre-lodgement review for some proposals, and written planning advice. General pre-lodgement meetings aren't described; call the Duty Planning Officer on 9273 6000.
